mainEntity.name: What should I prepare before consulting a contractor about detached living quarters?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before meeting with a remodeling contractor, gather your property survey, list your functional must-haves, and review your community rules. A boundary survey helps identify property lines, existing easements, and current structures, clarifying where new construction can legally sit. You should also outline your intended use: decide whether the space needs a full kitchen or a kitchenette, specific mobility accommodations like zero-threshold walk-in showers, or dedicated laundry hookups. If your property is governed by a homeowners association, obtain their architectural guidelines regarding accessory structures, exterior color schemes, and rooflines to ensure initial designs align with community standards.
acceptedAnswer.description: Collect your property survey, establish intended uses such as kitchens or accessible bathrooms, and check any HOA guidelines regarding setbacks and exterior styling.
